staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout, and the file/line anchors below are grounded in this tree. The staged checkout commit differs from the metadata vulnerable commit but still contains the unfixed `RTCM3_RECOGNIZED` length extraction later masked by fix commit `964806dd6dac70232ef1e39f31034b12e4517013`.

classification.classification_note: AddressSanitizer reports `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `gpsd/crc24q.c:157`. Source-grounded analysis of the exact witness shows that `packet_parse()` discards the leading `0xff` after the Zodiac false start, then recognizes the second `0xd3 00 00 20 20 20` as RTCM3, rescans the 7-byte buffer `D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`, breaks at `idx == 0`, computes `data_len == 0xD300` from unmasked bytes `D3 00`, and passes `&lexer->inbuffer[0]` plus that inflated length into `crc24q_hash()`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42527319 (gpsd): Stack-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target FuzzPacket [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42527319
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / gt_results/arvo_42527319/poc / trace_feedback.json / staged vulnerable source in gt_results/arvo_42527319/_work/src/gpsd / local git show of fix commit 964806dd6dac70232ef1e39f31034b12e4517013
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 10-byte file `20 20 FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`. `FuzzPacket` copies those bytes into stack `struct gps_lexer_t lexer` and calls `packet_parse()`. `packet_parse()` first discards the two leading spaces, leaving `FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`. In `GROUND_STATE`, `0xff` selects `ZODIAC_LEADER_1`. The following `0xd3` is not Zodiac's required `0x81`, so `nextstate()` at `packet.c:1372` calls `character_pushback(lexer, GROUND_STATE)` and rewinds to that same `0xd3`, but because the return value is ignored the function falls through to `return true` at `packet.c:1928`. `packet_parse()` therefore executes `case GROUND_STATE`, whose `character_discard()` removes the leading `0xff` and resets the live buffer to `D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`. The first RTCM3 candidate now starts at `inbuffer[0]`, but its header byte is another `0xd3`, so `RTCM3_LEADER_1` rejects it and pushes that second `0xd3` back. Re-reading the second `0xd3 00 00 20 20 20` reaches `RTCM3_RECOGNIZED` with a 7-byte buffer and `lexer->inbufptr - lexer->inbuffer == 7`. In `case RTCM3_RECOGNIZED`, the rescan loop starts at `inbuffer[0]`, breaks immediately at the earlier rejected `0xd3` (`idx == 0`), and computes `data_len` from the following bytes as `0xD300` because it combines the full next two bytes and never masks RTCM3's 10-bit length field. `crc24q_check(&lexer->inbuffer[0], data_len + 6)` then asks `crc24q_hash()` to read `54019` bytes from a 7-byte buffered slice inside the stack `lexer`, and the CRC loop eventually crosses the stack redzone, producing the saved AddressSanitizer crash at `gpsd/crc24q.c:157`. The fix resolves this witness by masking `data_len &= 0x03ff`; the additional `if (2048 < idx) idx = 0;` hunk is not exercised by this path.

source.description: First project-code statement on the crashing path that consumes the witness into parser-dispatch state by classifying the post-space `0xff` byte as a Zodiac leader.
source.value_from: The exact staged witness `gt_results/arvo_42527319/poc` (sha256 `8129a28b2a3ecd00d5efbab10d17676cc8065bbf90f119cb37a50b1c6d61d59a`) is the raw 10-byte buffer `20 20 FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`. After earlier `GROUND_STATE` discards remove the two leading `0x20` bytes, the next attacker-controlled byte is `0xff` at `lexer->inbuffer[0]`, and this statement turns it into `ZODIAC_LEADER_1` state for the false-start path that follows.

root_cause.description: Root cause. Once `packet_parse()` rescans the recognized buffer and chooses `idx == 0`, this assignment forms `data_len` from the full next two bytes without enforcing RTCM3's 10-bit length field. The actual recognized leader byte `0xd3` at `inbuffer[1]` is therefore misused as the high length byte, yielding `data_len == 0xD300`.
root_cause.note: The fix commit adds `data_len &= 0x03ff` at this site. Its separate `if (2048 < idx) idx = 0;` hunk is not needed for this witness because the rescan breaks immediately at `idx == 0`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. The CRC loop dereferences `data[i]` while `i` is driven by the inflated length derived after `packet_parse()` rescans from `idx == 0` and misinterprets the next `0xd3` as length data, so the read eventually leaves the stack `lexer` object.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved AddressSanitizer report is `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `gpsd/crc24q.c:157:35` with stack `crc24q_hash -> crc24q_check -> packet_parse -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` and says the invalid read overflows stack variable `lexer` in `fuzzer/FuzzPacket.c`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This assignment materializes the concrete oversized CRC length input `data_len == 0xD300` from bytes `D3 00` after the recognized-case rescan stops at `idx == 0`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: With the recognized buffer `D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`, `idx == 0` makes `lexer->inbuffer[1] == 0xD3` and `lexer->inbuffer[2] == 0x00`, which this statement combines into `0xD300`.
tainted_value_origin.note: The RTCM3 length field is only 10 bits wide; the high six bits of the first length byte should not survive into `data_len`.

zodiac_false_start.description: At `ZODIAC_LEADER_1`, seeing `0xd3` instead of `0x81` rewinds `inbufptr` to that same `0xd3` and restores `GROUND_STATE`. Because this branch ignores the helper's `false` return, `nextstate()` later falls through to `return true`, so `packet_parse()` executes `case GROUND_STATE` and discards the leading `0xff`.

first_rtcm3_header_rejected.description: The first RTCM3 leader candidate begins at `inbuffer[0]`, but its following header byte is another `0xd3`, so the six-zero-bit check fails and this pushback rewinds to `inbuffer[1]` for a second leader attempt.

parser_admitted.description: After the second `0xd3 00 00 20 20 20` sequence is re-read, the third payload decrement reaches `RTCM3_RECOGNIZED` with live buffer `D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20` and `lexer->inbufptr - lexer->inbuffer == 7`.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation; the chain is reconstructed from the staged vulnerable source plus the saved PoC and sanitizer artifacts only.

The saved run used `lexer.errout.debug = 0`, so Stage 01 did not preserve a runtime packet dump. The post-discard buffer `D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`, the recognized-case rescan index `idx == 0`, and the `&lexer->inbuffer[0]` CRC start pointer are therefore derived statically from the exact witness and the staged `nextstate()` / `packet_parse()` / `character_discard()` control flow.

The local staged checkout at `gt_results/arvo_42527319/_work/src/gpsd` is on commit `97733d06e933132de3267b0c22aeb5dc0546e640`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit` `5fb88bc7be83ca16f8136dcedc29ddf04153b665`. The line anchors below are resolved against the staged vulnerable tree.

No standalone `reproduction_report.json` was present under the result directory, and the metadata `patch_path` did not exist locally. This GT therefore used `poc`, `sanitizer_trace.txt`, `default_crash_trace.txt`, `trace_feedback.json`, and `git show 964806dd6dac70232ef1e39f31034b12e4517013 -- gpsd/packet.c` from the staged checkout.

The fix commit also adds an `idx > 2048` reset before length extraction. The saved witness grounds only the length-mask hunk as necessary because the recognized-case rescan breaks immediately at `idx == 0`.

coarse_trace.summary: After two leading spaces are discarded, `0xff` selects `ZODIAC_LEADER_1`; the following `0xd3` triggers the false-start pushback, `nextstate()` still returns true, and `case GROUND_STATE` discards the leading `0xff`, leaving `D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`.

The parser first treats `inbuffer[0]` as an RTCM3 leader candidate, rejects it because the next byte is another `0xd3`, then re-reads that second `0xd3 00 00 20 20 20` sequence and reaches `RTCM3_RECOGNIZED`.

In `RTCM3_RECOGNIZED`, the rescan starts at the 7-byte buffer `D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`, stops immediately at `idx == 0`, and forms `data_len == 0xD300` from bytes `D3 00` because the code does not mask the 10-bit RTCM3 length.

`crc24q_check(&lexer->inbuffer[0], 54022)` forwards `54019` bytes into the CRC loop, which reads beyond the 7-byte buffered slice and eventually beyond the stack-resident `lexer` object, producing the saved AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.note: Source. After earlier `GROUND_STATE` discards remove the two leading spaces, the live bytes are `FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`; consuming the current `0xff` in `GROUND_STATE` classifies the witness into `ZODIAC_LEADER_1` dispatch state.

Reading the following `0xd3` under `ZODIAC_LEADER_1`, this false-start branch rewinds `inbufptr` from `&lexer->inbuffer[2]` to `&lexer->inbuffer[1]` and restores `GROUND_STATE`, but it does not remove the leading `0xff` yet.

Because step 2 ignores the helper's `false` return, `nextstate()` falls through to this `return true` instead of propagating a pushback failure. `packet_parse()` therefore does not take its `continue` path for this byte.

depends_on.via: the Zodiac false-start branch does not `return character_pushback(...)`

fine_trace.note: Invoked from `packet_parse()` `case GROUND_STATE`, this discard removes the leading `0xff`, decrements `inbuflen` from 8 to 7, resets `inbufptr` to `lexer->inbuffer`, and leaves the live buffer `D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`.

depends_on.via: the leading byte to discard is still `0xff`

fine_trace.note: With the discarded buffer now starting `D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`, the next iteration consumes `inbuffer[0] == 0xd3` in `GROUND_STATE` and starts the first RTCM3 leader attempt at that earlier byte.

The following header byte for that first candidate is another `0xd3`, so `RTCM3_LEADER_1` fails its `0 == (c & 0xFC)` check, rewinds `inbufptr` from `&lexer->inbuffer[2]` to `&lexer->inbuffer[1]`, and restores `GROUND_STATE`.

depends_on.via: the next buffered byte is `0xd3`, so `c & 0xFC` is nonzero

fine_trace.note: Because step 6 returned `false`, the next loop iteration re-consumes the pushed-back second `0xd3` at `inbuffer[1]` in `GROUND_STATE` and starts the actual RTCM3 leader attempt that will be recognized.
Reading the next byte `0x00` under `RTCM3_LEADER_1`, this statement stores the RTCM3 high length bits as zero and advances to `RTCM3_LEADER_2`.

depends_on.via: the header byte after the actual leader is `0x00`

fine_trace.code:
lexer->length |= c;
lexer->length += 3;     // to get the three checksum bytes
fine_trace.note: The following byte `0x00` supplies the low length bits, and adding the three checksum bytes makes `lexer->length == 3`, so exactly the remaining three `0x20` bytes are enough to finish this zero-length RTCM3 packet.

depends_on.via: lexer->length == 0 before OR-ing the low byte

fine_trace.note: As the three trailing `0x20` bytes are consumed in `RTCM3_PAYLOAD`, the third decrement drives `lexer->length` from 1 to 0 and sets `lexer->state = RTCM3_RECOGNIZED`, reaching recognition with `lexer->inbufptr - lexer->inbuffer == 7` and live buffer `D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`.

In `case RTCM3_RECOGNIZED`, this rescan examines the 7 buffered bytes `D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20` from `inbuffer[0]` and breaks immediately at `idx == 0`. That selects the earlier rejected leader candidate instead of the actual recognized packet start at `inbuffer[1]`.

Using `idx == 0`, this statement misinterprets the actual recognized leader `0xd3` at `inbuffer[1]` as the high length byte and `0x00` at `inbuffer[2]` as the low byte, storing `data_len == 0xD300` (54016). RTCM3 length is only 10 bits, but the vulnerable code keeps the high six bits; the fix commit masks them off here.

This call pairs start pointer `&lexer->inbuffer[0]` with claimed packet span `54022`. Only 7 buffered bytes remain from that pointer to the current `inbufptr`, but no pre-call check clamps the inflated `data_len` to the available RTCM3 bytes.

The CRC helper strips the trailer and asks `crc24q_hash()` to consume `54019` bytes. That bound already exceeds both the 7-byte buffered RTCM slice from step 13 and the `inbuffer` array inside the stack `lexer` object that AddressSanitizer later names.

Sink. The hash loop continues while `i < len`; with `len == 54019`, the `data[i]` dereference eventually advances beyond the stack-resident `lexer` object and into the redzone, matching the saved AddressSanitizer `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at this line.

depends_on.via: the loop condition `i < len` keeps advancing the read

allocation_context.note: ASan reports that the invalid read overflows the stack variable `lexer` allocated in this frame; the frame contains `[32, 46440) 'lexer'` and `[46704, 93112) 'lexer2'`.

crash_stack.function: fuzzer::FuzzerDriver(int*, char***, int (*)(unsigned char const*, unsigned long))

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the crash by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42527319 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which reported `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow` at `gpsd/crc24q.c:157` while `FuzzPacket` processed this exact file.

format.name: raw 10-byte lexer input buffer
format.contract: Exactly the 10-byte witness stored in `gt_results/arvo_42527319/poc`: `20 20 FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`. It must still let `packet_parse()` discard the two leading `0x20` bytes, take `0xff d3` through `ZODIAC_LEADER_1`'s false branch, then execute `GROUND_STATE`'s `character_discard()` so the live buffer becomes `D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`. The first RTCM3 candidate at `inbuffer[0]` must be rejected by the second `0xd3` header byte, the second `0xd3` must then be re-read as the recognized leader, and `RTCM3_RECOGNIZED` must rescan from `inbuffer[0]`, stop immediately at `idx == 0`, compute `data_len == 0xD300` from bytes `D3 00`, and call `crc24q_check(&lexer->inbuffer[0], 54022)`. The staged artifacts do not prove a broader class of duplicated-`0xd3` RTCM3 prefixes beyond this exact witness.
